newsitem.title: UK: Cargo 2000 outlines issues, details members.
newsitem.headline: Cargo 2000 outlines issues, details members.

text.p: Airlines and freight forwarders represented in the Cargo 2000 task force to speed air freight handling have now formally agreed its objectives, a Cargo 2000 statement said.

The task force was launched at the International Air Transport Association's(IATA) Cargo Week 1997 in Long Beach, California and followed a meeting beteen major airlines and freight forwarders in Paris last September.
The statement said the four key issues facing the task force are:
- Mapping of the air cargo business processes;
- Identification of the elements of the processes where quality can be improved and costs reduced;
- Actioning necessary procedures to secure these improvements;
- The development of an immediate plan to implement electronic data interchange(EDI) messaging, including the electronic airway bill, tracking and tracing, and bar code labelling

Cargo 2000's executive steering group has held initial meetings in the past week in London and Frankfurt. Its next session is expected to be in about two months, probably in the U.S, an industry source said.
The statement said that 15 airlines and 13 forwarders are initial members of Cargo 2000, while other airlines and forwarders have requested information and expressed interest in joining.

Cargo 2000 has set minimum criteria for membership for both airlines and forwarders. These relate to members' EDI capability, including the ability to dispatch and receive messages electronically and bar code labelling, it added.

It said that James Hartigan of United Airlines vice-president cargo was elected chairman of the executive committee with Klaus Geissler, managing director of Schenker International as vice-chairman. Other members are Gunter Rohrmann (AEI); Kevin Hatton of British Airways World Cargo); James Barrington of Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd; Jean Godart of Kuehne & Nagel ); Wilhelm Althen, Lufthansa Cargo ; Hwang Teng Aun from Singapore Airlines ) and Hiroshi Takahashi from Yusen Air & Sea Services ).
The group has appointed John Hartnett as Project Director on a consultancy basis, the statement added.

Hartigan, who is also UAL's vice-president cargo, said: "We believe that the time is now right ..... to develop within a set time frame best practice, process and service deliveries for the industry worldwide. A detailed work plan is now being developed by the executive committee and we will announce details in due course."

Schenker International managing director, Klaus Geissler , added: "For the first time, major airlines and forwarders are taking the initiative to solve existing industry problems such as quality and EDI in all its facets, in order to deliver to their customers the high quality, fast, reliable and cost effective product they have demanded for such a long time.
"Other important aspects of the industry, such as the airline/forwarder relationship, will also be much improved through this forum. We have a lot of hope for the project."

Member airlines are Aer Lingus, Alitalia, American Airlines Austrian Airlines, British Airways , Cargolux, Cathay Pacific, Delta Airlines, Japan Airlines Co Ltd, Korean Air Lines, Lufthansa Cargo; South African Airways, Singapore Airlines, Swissair and UAL.

Forwarder members are Air Express International, Danzas, Emery Worldwide, Fritz, Kintetsu, Kuehne & Nagel, Lemuir Express, Nippon Express Panalpina, Schenker International, Scac Delmas Vieljeux(SDV) and Yusen Air & Sea Services. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+5017
